Kernel row sums and spatially lagged gene1, for every bandwidth

Source: R/RcppExports.R
moran_kernel_pass.Rd

Internal. Computes, for each bandwidth h, the row sums of the kernel weight matrix and the vector v_h = K(h) (gene1 / rowsum(h)) which the caller contracts with gene2.

moran_kernel_pass(
  coords,
  gene1,
  h_vec,
  eps = 0,
  kernel = "gaussian",
  dist_method = "euclidean",
  drop_isolated = TRUE,
  n_threads = 1L,
  rowsums_only = FALSE,
  p = 2
)

Arguments

coords

N x 2 numeric matrix of coordinates.

gene1

Length-N numeric vector, already centred and scaled.

h_vec

Numeric vector of bandwidths.

eps

Weights are kept when w > eps, and excluded from the row sum otherwise. eps = 0 keeps every non-underflowed weight, which is the documented default and the condition under which this reduces exactly to the reference implementation.

kernel

"gaussian", "uniform" or "exponential".

dist_method

"euclidean", "manhattan" or "minkowski".

drop_isolated

When TRUE, cells with a zero row sum contribute nothing rather than producing a non-finite value. The caller uses this to implement nan_policy.

n_threads

Requested OpenMP threads; ignored when built without OpenMP support.

rowsums_only

When TRUE, skip the second pass and return the full row sum matrix instead of V. Used by qc_neighborhoods(), which needs the neighbourhood sizes but not the lagged gene.

p

Order of the Minkowski distance; ignored by the other metrics.

Value

A list with V (n_h x N) or rowsums (n_h x N), plus rowsum_mean, rowsum_min, n_isolated and h.
